content.title: About
content.content: Ready‑to‑serve marinara sauce is a classic Italian tomato sauce flavored with basil, oregano and garlic, designed for quick preparation of spaghetti. It is made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil and herbs, contains no preservatives and is ready to use straight from the jar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “marinara” comes from the Italian verb “marinare” meaning “to season”, not from the sea.
Traditional marinara is meat‑free, making it suitable for vegetarians.
Tomatoes used in the sauce are often grown in sunny Mediterranean regions where they reach peak flavor.
Marinara sauce is a common base for pizza, lasagna and many other Italian dishes.
Once opened, the sauce can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 7 days.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The sauce uses a modest amount of olive oil, making it a low‑calorie option for weight‑conscious meals.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomatoes and herbs supply vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and enhances iron absorption from plant foods.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Tomatoes contain dietary fiber that promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or the herbs used in the sauce.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ready‑to‑serve sauces can be high in salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Preservatives in some versions
items.content: Certain commercial products may contain preservatives; choose a preservative‑free option if you have a sensitive stomach.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Heat the sauce in a saucepan or microwave, add cooked spaghetti and toss. Top with grated Parmesan, fresh basil or olives if desired. The sauce also works well in casseroles, on pizza, or as a dip for bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep it refrigerated and use within 7 days. Discard if the sauce develops off‑odors, discoloration or mold.
